combinationRules.effect: Concurrent use of a renin–angiotensin system inhibitor, diuretic and NSAID has been associated with acute kidney injury. A 2026 nationwide study found the main risk signal with diuretic plus NSAID use, varying by diuretic class. Ask a pharmacist or prescriber to review it; this check cannot assess kidney function, hydration, dose or duration.

source.publisher: Journal of Pharmaceutical Health Care and Sciences
source.title: Drug-specific risks of acute kidney injury associated with triple whammy therapy: a nationwide self-controlled case series study in Japan
source.attribution: Kunitsu Y, Abe R, Ikuta K, Hira D, Nakagawa S, Tsuda M, Terada T. J Pharm Health Care Sci. 2026;12:42. doi:10.1186/s40780-026-00560-8. CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Rule wording summarized and independently written.
source.currentnessNote: 2026 nationwide self-controlled case series using Japanese claims data; population and health system may differ from New Zealand. The study found the main risk signal with diuretic plus NSAID exposure and variation by diuretic class; it does not predict an individual's risk.

combinationRules.evidenceSummary: A 2026 nationwide Japanese self-controlled case series (92,880 people) examined acute kidney injury across renin–angiotensin system inhibitor, diuretic, and NSAID exposure. Its main risk signal was diuretic plus NSAID use, with risk varying by diuretic class. It does not estimate an individual New Zealand patient's risk or prove causation.
